state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process` is green: `run` and `spawn` have all their feature proofs, and the group's dossier check passes. `Core\Process\Handle` has its class card and `kill` has all its proofs. `readStdout`, `readStderr`, `writeStdin` and `wait` still owe everything but their cards, and those cards are still in the old voice. `Core\Process\Result`, `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue` are untouched and still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

A Unix-only example is run by hand under WSL: rebuild with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl cargo build` from `/mnt/d/mwl`, then `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run --config <dir>/nvs.toml <file>`, each through a script under `.agent-tmp/` because `wsl.exe -- bash -lc` mangles nested quotes. Write the `.out` from that run and `cmp` it. The attacks and benches run on both platforms: they pick `/bin/echo` / `/usr/bin/yes` or `cmd.exe` by `Core\Path::SEPARATOR`. `benches/members/core/Process/nvs.toml` and `benches/members/core/Process-Handle/nvs.toml` are shared by every bench in their class. `false as string` prints nothing, so an attack prints a word for a boolean.

`?bytes as string` used to throw on well-formed text. It now validates UTF-8 the way `bytes as string` does (`Helper::TaggedAsString`). So a chunk from `readStdout` converts without a `!= null` narrowing first.
